23.t: Working with data: flu vaccine effectiveness
q: Calculate the mean effectiveness for all ages.
Explain why the vaccine worked poorly in season B.
The virus changed its surface antigens (antigenic drift) after the vaccine strains were chosen, so antibodies made after vaccination bind poorly to the new virus.
Explain why a new flu vaccine is needed every year.
Flu is an RNA virus with a high mutation rate, so its surface proteins (haemagglutinin, neuraminidase) keep changing.
A student says the vaccine was "useless" in season D. Evaluate this claim.
39% fewer cases among millions of vaccinated people prevents many illnesses, hospital stays and deaths, and slows spread. It does not protect everyone, but it is far from useless.
Suggest why effectiveness is lower in people over 65.
The immune system weakens with age, so vaccination produces fewer antibodies and memory cells.
